Big Question
Today’s Wonder

Ransom has run from the ruler of Malacandra since the day he landed. What if the thing you fear most has been inviting you as a guest all along?

🎯
Objectives
By the end of this lesson…
🎵Craft: I can hear alliteration and say what a repeated sound does.
🏝️Reading: I can follow Ransom across Meldilorn and explain, from the carvings and the Oyarsa’s story, why Earth is called the silent planet.
🔭Inference: I can explain what Ransom feared and what was really waiting for him.

🎵 Alliteration

Professor Lovelore Literature expert

🎵 Alliteration

The repeating of the same first sound in words that sit close together.

📖 Lewis, Chapter 17

“Depth, dimness, softness and perspective were returning to the landscape.”

👂 Sound, not spelling

sunk and shattered share a letter, not a sound.

What do you notice first: what a sentence says, or how it sounds?
2
✏️ Fix the Sentence
Capitals and a comma
✅ Correct model
When the bell rang, the professor closed her book.

A part of a sentence that cannot stand alone, such as when the bell rang, is a dependent clause. When it opens a sentence, a comma comes after it. Names of particular people and places start with a capital letter. Use the model to fix the sentence below.

🔧 Fix this one
Tap a word to capitalize it. Tap the small circle after a word to add a comma, then a period, then nothing.

Ozymandias
Percy Bysshe Shelley (1818) · Lines 1–5 of 14
I met a traveller from an antique land Who said: Two vast and trunkless legs of stone Stand in the desert...Near them, on the sand, Half sunk, a shattered visage lies, whose frown, And wrinkled lip, and sneer of cold command,
antique: very old, ancient · trunkless: without the body; only the legs are left · visage: face · sneer of cold command: the scornful look of a man used to giving orders
The hard c in cold command sounds…

🎓 Questions from Professor Lovelore
She asks. You answer.
0 / 3
Professor Lovelore
Here is my first question. On the island, Ransom walks all the way round without going up to the grove or down to the crowd. Why does he keep his distance?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Next. On the carved stone, Ransom finds the Sun, then Mercury, then Venus. What has been done to the third world?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore
Last question. The Oyarsa says that if the men had come a few miles to see him, he would have received them with honour. What does that tell you about their whole voyage?
Your answer
Professor Lovelore

Good. Look at what your answers share: a stranger afraid of being seen, a world with its light cut away, and two men who crossed millions of miles to avoid a short walk.

Lewis lets you hear the Oyarsa arrive, too: “like all that is stillest and smallest and most hard to seize in nature.” Stillest, smallest, seize. That is alliteration, and here it hushes you the way the island hushed Ransom.

Now walk the island yourself.

🖋️ Why Silent?
Written in your own words
Augray could only hint at why our world is silent. The stone shows the Earth’s figure gone, and the Oyarsa tells the story. In two sentences, explain why the hnau call our world the silent planet.

The hnau call our world the silent planet because… The Oyarsa says…

Type your answers here. Everything you type this week is saved and gathered into one Week 5 Work PDF at the end of the fourth lesson. First, three questions on Chapters 17 and 18. Then copy one sentence the Oyarsa speaks.

Part 1Chapter ThinkingComplete sentences, with a detail from the text.
1. Ransom feels that “the island was having a look at him” and, later, that he is being looked at “by things that had a right to look” (Chapter 17). What is that feeling, and how is it different from his old fear of monsters?
Show a starter

The feeling is… It is different from his old fear because…

2. The pfifltrigg carves Ransom as a thick, squat figure and says, “Too like, and they will not believe it” (Chapter 17). What does the carving show about how one kind of creature sees another?
Show a starter

The carving shows that a creature sees another kind… I can tell because…

3. The Oyarsa tells Ransom, “These are not the real reasons,” and says Ransom has spent his whole time on Malacandra running from him (Chapter 18). Was Ransom’s fear reasonable? Use one thing he could not have known.
Show a starter

Ransom’s fear was (or was not) reasonable because… He could not have known…

Part 2CopyworkCopy exactly, then look closely at one mark or one sound.
📌 Watch how
Jonah’s copywork
Jonah · 8th Grade Scholar

Sentence: “Those are not great reasons,” said the voice. (Chapter 18)

One mark: The comma inside the quotation marks lets the Oyarsa’s words finish softly before “said the voice” takes over; a full stop there would make him sound clipped instead of patient.

Choose one sentence the Oyarsa speaks in Chapter 18. Copy it exactly from your own copy, punctuation and all.
In one sentence, say what one mark or one sound in your sentence does.
